# TinyChannels v0.1.38 public-writer fixture

`records.json` was generated by the public storage writers in the released
TinyChannels `v0.1.38` source tag (`9e1a340bf8f2cf89d5dd713a557b2c1a6c2406d6`).
That release's unchanged `Cargo.toml` and `Cargo.lock` resolve
`tinystoragedrivers-core` to tag `v1.0.0`, commit
`141fd9ed0ad5d14a8fb5a1b3e837a719e81ac08d`. The fixture exercises the public
delivery queue/result and remote session store APIs; it is not a hand-authored
record file. The separate `migrations_tests.rs` seeds historical underscore
collection layouts to exercise those schema transforms.

To regenerate from a clean checkout, fetch the exact tag, initialize its
submodules, copy this directory's `generate.rs` to
`examples/generate_v1_fixture.rs`, then run
`cargo run --locked --example generate_v1_fixture > records.json`. The
generator writes to the released in-memory storage backend and emits the
persisted records. TSD host-owned `created_ms` values (and result expiry based
on generation time) vary between regenerations; tests validate application
payloads and schema/expiry behavior without pinning those clock-dependent
metadata values.

For example, from the TinyChannels checkout containing this fixture:

```sh
archive="$(mktemp -d)/tinychannels-v0.1.38"
git clone --branch v0.1.38 --recurse-submodules https://github.com/tinyhumansai/tinychannels.git "$archive"
git -C "$archive" checkout --detach 9e1a340bf8f2cf89d5dd713a557b2c1a6c2406d6
cp tests/fixtures/legacy-v0.1.38/generate.rs "$archive/examples/generate_v1_fixture.rs"
(cd "$archive" && cargo run --locked --example generate_v1_fixture > records.json)
sha256sum "$archive/records.json"
```

The checked-in fixture SHA-256 is
`e18541965b15efbf667da89e0a9106fb8b4e2b8cf5e6fac01af5a3d7511732f8`.
